messages.subject: kmeans issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi;

I was wondering if someone might be able to help me out please?

I am working through the book Predictive Analytics with Rattle and QlikSense, and have reached the chapter on Clustering. The dataset in the book has 440 rows, but when I run the clustering algorithm it returns only 308 results?

The spreadsheet is .csv, and the summary report comes back with the correct number of rows, and I am stumped!

Any help greatly appreciated.

John

messages.subject: RE: kmeans issue [SEC=UNCLASSIFIED]
messages.body_plain:

messages.subject: Re: kmeans issue [SEC=UNCLASSIFIED]
messages.body_plain:
Hi Graham;

The dataset comes from the book, and can be found here: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets/Wholesale+customers#

After downloading the file and opening R and Rattle, in the "Data" tab I:
1. Select .csv file;
2. Upload .csv file using Execute;
3. Select "Ignore" for variables 1 Channel and 2 Region;
4. Execute;
5. In "Explore" tab I make sure "Summary" and "Summary" are both selected;
6. Execute.

That's when I find that Rattle has only "seen" 308 observations.

When I go to the "Cluster" tab, I:

1. Select "KMeans",
2. Number of clusters: 10;
3. No Re-scale;
4. Select Iterate Clusters;
5. Execute;
The plot produced is different to the book because the peak is at 5 instead of 6, but I continue to follow the book and
6. Select Number of Clusters: 6;
7. Deselect Iterate Clusters
8. Select Runs: 10
9. Execute
10. Go to "Evaluate" tab
11. Select KMeans, Training, and All
This produces a .csv with a kmeans column filled for 308 rows.

I have downloaded the file a couple of times, but have not achieved any different results?

Thanks for your help, all the best,

John

messages.subject: Re: kmeans issue [SEC=UNCLASSIFIED]
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

On the Data tab you have Partition enabled. This is what Tony Nolan was referring to. By default Rattle will partition the dataset into train/evaluate/test with 70% chosen for the training dataset: 0.7 * 440 = 308. Uncheck the Partition option to use the whole dataset.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject_clean: Decision tree - node labels font size
messages.body_plain:
Hi Carlos,

The short answer is no, not directly in Rattle.

However, the plot is generated underneath using rattle::fancyRpartPlot(). Have a look at the Log tab for the actual command used. This in turn uses rpart.plot::prp() and you can pass various tuning parameters to this function. Have a look at

> ?rpart.plot::prp

for details of the parameters.

So to test this you can generate the plot in Rattle and then copy the fancyRpartPlot() command from the Log tab into the R Console and then experiment:

> fancyRpartPlot(crs$rpart, main="Decision Tree")
> fancyRpartPlot(crs$rpart, main="Decision Tree", cex=1)
> fancyRpartPlot(crs$rpart, main="Decision Tree", tweak=1.5)

etc to change the font size.

Regards,
Graham
